summary: The diff replaces the not-implemented throw at step 5 with a call to the public JSON.parse entry (`parse::parse`) with no reviver, and discards the result as the spec does (step 9 uses jsonString, not the parse result). No special-casing, no swallowed errors, no made-up values, no changes outside raw_json.rs. The 4 newly passing tests fit the change (SyntaxError and creation paths). The remaining failures (basic.js, bigint-raw-json-can-be-stringified.js) depend on JSON.stringify handling [[IsRawJSON]], which is outside this ticket. Steps 1-4 and the rest of the function are unchanged in this diff, so I could not verify steps 9-10 (CreateDataPropertyOrThrow, SetIntegrityLevel frozen) from the visible text. Equivalence check: with no reviver, JSON.parse performs ToString (a no-op on a String), ParseJSON, then returns the value unchanged, which matches ParseJSON(jsonString) here. The first and last code-unit checks exclude `{`, `[` and leading/trailing whitespace, so the parse result is always a primitive, consistent with the step 6 assertion.
notes_for_next_attempt: Nothing blocking. Optional cleanup: expose parse_json as pub(crate) in json/parse.rs and call it directly, which matches the spec's ParseJSON name more closely and avoids routing through the JSON.parse entry point. The workaround is behaviourally equivalent for this call. The JSON.stringify IsRawJSON handling needed for basic.js and bigint-raw-json-can-be-stringified.js belongs to a different ticket.
